paper.title_en: Observation of rotonic density enhancement at the boundary of a uniform dipolar superfluid
paper.abstract_en: The collective excitations of a quantum liquid lie at the heart of its emergent behaviour. In many systems, the variation of excitation energy ${\varepsilon}$ with wavevector $k$ exhibits a softening at a characteristic lengthscale, which plays a key role in thermodynamics and transport. These excitations, termed rotons, often reflect an underlying tendency of the liquid to crystallize into a competing symmetry-broken state, such as the solid state of helium or the Wigner crystal of electrons in a magnetic field. More than $50$ years ago, it was predicted that rotons should manifest as emergent density oscillations at the fluid's boundary, but this effect has not been observed. Here, we realize an ultracold dipolar superfluid confined in a homogeneous trapping potential and directly confirm the emergence of rotonic density enhancement at its edge. This is accompanied by rotonic density fluctuations across the bulk, which are linked to the static edge structure via the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. Increasing the dipolar character leads to an azimuthal density modulation of the fluid's boundary, which we show to be analogous to the behaviour of a quasi-one-dimensional fluid confined in an annular optical potential.
